hook: In 1848 an explosion drove an iron rod through the front of railroad foreman Phineas Gage's head. He survived, walked and talked, but friends said he was "no longer Gage": impulsive and hard to work with. Cases like his gave the first clues that particular parts of the brain do particular jobs.

prereq.q: Which part of a neuron is wrapped in myelin?
prereq.why: Myelin wraps the axon and speeds the action potential.

prereq.q: A study changes nothing and simply examines one unusual person in depth. What method is it?
prereq.why: A case study looks at one person or a few people in depth.

prereq.q: A researcher removes participants' names and uses code numbers. Which safeguard is this?
prereq.why: Keeping data from being linked to a person protects confidentiality.

chain.cause: Signals from the eyes, ears and skin reach the brain
chain.effect: the thalamus relays them to the right areas of the cortex (smell is the exception)

chain.cause: The occipital, temporal and parietal lobes process vision, hearing and touch
chain.effect: association areas combine the pieces into meaning

chain.cause: The frontal lobe plans an action
chain.effect: the motor cortex sends commands to the opposite side of the body, and the cerebellum makes the movement smooth

chain.cause: Damage to one region removes or weakens its job
chain.effect: patterns of loss (lesions, strokes, split-brain surgery) reveal what each region does

ideas: The brainstem keeps you alive: the medulla runs breathing and heart rate, and the reticular activating system controls arousal. The cerebellum coordinates balance and smooth movement.

Four lobes of the cerebral cortex: frontal (planning, judgment; the motor cortex; Broca's area for producing speech), parietal (touch, in the somatosensory cortex), occipital (vision), temporal (hearing; Wernicke's area for understanding speech).
Limbic structures: the thalamus relays senses, the hypothalamus keeps homeostasis and directs the pituitary, the hippocampus forms new memories, the amygdala handles fear.
Each hemisphere controls the opposite side of the body. The corpus callosum links them; split-brain cases show that language is mostly in the left hemisphere in most people.
Tools: case studies of damage, lesions in animal research, EEG (when, from the scalp) and fMRI (where, from blood flow). The brain rewires through neuroplasticity.

misconception.wrong: People are either left-brained (logical) or right-brained (creative).
misconception.right: The hemispheres specialize for some tasks, but they work together through the corpus callosum. Brain-imaging studies of large groups find no left-brain or right-brain types of people.

summary: The brainstem keeps you alive and alert, the cerebellum smooths movement, and the limbic structures handle relay, drives, memory and fear. The cortex has four lobes, each with its own jobs, including the motor and somatosensory strips and the two language areas. Each hemisphere controls the opposite side of the body, and the corpus callosum links them. We know this from damage cases, lesions, EEG and fMRI, and the brain can rewire through neuroplasticity.
